summary: Defines two more kinds of revocation information that the Cryptographic Message Syntax can carry: Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) responses and Server-Based Certificate Validation Protocol (SCVP) requests and responses. CRLs were already supported. It is a Proposed Standard.

eli5.summary: A way to attach a note, 'this ID card has been cancelled', in more formats than just the old list.

questions: how to carry ocsp response in cms
subtitle: Lets a CMS message carry OCSP and SCVP answers about revoked certificates, not just CRLs.

tldr.problem: The Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS) could carry revocation information, but Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs) were the only format with a defined place in the message.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5940 uses CMS's existing 'other' choice to carry two more formats, each tagged with an object identifier under a new id-ri arc: OCSP responses, and SCVP requests plus responses.
tldr.outcome: Applications can bundle OCSP or SCVP results with signed or encrypted content. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 5940 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It remains the definition of how OCSP responses and SCVP requests and responses are placed in CMS revocation information.

sections.title: Why CMS Needs More Revocation Formats
sections.content:
The RevocationInfoChoices type defined in RFC 5652 lets revocation information travel inside the SignedData, EnvelopedData, AuthenticatedData and AuthEnvelopedData content types. The goal is to give a receiver enough information to decide whether the certificates and attribute certificates in the protected content have been revoked.

X.509 CRLs are the primary source of revocation status information, but the CMS design lets any other format be supported. This RFC specifies two: Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) responses and Server-Based Certificate Validation Protocol (SCVP) requests and responses. It also notes that there may be more revocation status information than necessary, or less.
sections.eli5: When you send a signed message, you can staple proof that the sender's ID is still good. This RFC adds two new kinds of proof you can staple.

sections.title: The RevocationInfoChoices Structure
sections.content:
A RevocationInfoChoices is a set of RevocationInfoChoice values. Each is either a crl (a CertificateList) or an other value of type OtherRevocationInfoFormat. That type pairs an object identifier, otherRevInfoFormat, with data, otherRevInfo, whose type depends on the identifier.

The RFC says the other choice MUST be used to carry OCSP responses, SCVP requests and SCVP responses.

The RFC defines the id-ri arc, under the PKIX arc, for these formats. Numbers 1 and 3 were assigned to CRL and Delta CRL. They are not used because those formats already travel in the crl choice.
sections.eli5: The message has a slot for the standard form and a 'something else' slot. Each item in the 'something else' slot carries a label that says what kind of thing it is.

sections.title: Carrying an OCSP Response
sections.content:
To carry an OCSP response, otherRevInfoFormat is set to id-ri-ocsp-response, which is { id-ri 2 }. The otherRevInfo field MUST then hold the response as the OCSPResponse type defined in RFC 2560.

Two constraints apply. The responseStatus field MUST be successful, and the responseBytes field MUST be present. In other words, an error response has no place in the message.
sections.eli5: If you attach an OCSP answer, it has to be a real answer that says 'here is the result', not a note that says 'something went wrong'.

sections.title: Carrying SCVP Requests and Responses
sections.content:
SCVP is defined in RFC 5055. Unlike OCSP, SCVP permits unprotected and protected responses, and protected ones can be digitally signed or carry message authentication codes. That flexibility complicates things when someone other than the original requester validates the response. An unprotected response leaves a third party unable to know it came over a protected connection. A message authentication code cannot be checked by a third party who lacks the necessary key. So SCVP responses sent to a third party MUST be signed by the SCVP server.

Validating an SCVP response means matching it to its request, so the request MUST always be included with the response. The request need not be protected for this, since nonces and certIds can be checked.

The format is identified by id-ri-scvp, which is { id-ri 4 }, and the data is an SCVPReqRes sequence. The request field holds the unprotected, authenticated or signed request, and MUST be present if the response does not include the requestRef fullRequest field. The response field MUST hold the signed response with responseStatus of okay. Unprotected and authenticated responses MUST NOT be included.
sections.eli5: If you show someone else an answer from a helper, the answer has to carry the helper's signature and the original question, so they can trust it and see what it was answering.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of the CMS, OCSP and SCVP specifications, and of the ASN.1 module documents RFC 5911 and RFC 5912, apply.

The RFC adds one point. To store an unprotected or authenticated SCVP response locally, a client can wrap it in a SignedData. Whether another entity treats such a client-signed response as valid is a matter of local policy.
sections.eli5: If you keep a copy of a note and sign it yourself, whether other people believe it is up to them.

sections.title: IANA and ASN.1 Modules
sections.content:
The object identifiers come from an arc delegated by IANA to the PKIX Working Group. When that group closes, the arc and its registration procedures will be transferred to IANA. No further action by IANA is necessary for this document.

Appendix A gives the ASN.1. Appendix A.1 is a normative module for compilers that support the 1988 ASN.1. Appendix A.2 is an informative module in the 2002 ASN.1 notation. It carries the same information, and A.1 takes precedence if they conflict.
sections.eli5: The special label numbers are handed out from a list the standards group keeps, and nothing new needs to be registered.
